title: The Name of God
blurb: Follow the divine Name from the burning bush to Jesus' own "I AM" in the Gospel of John.

steps.title: A Voice from the Bush
steps.intro: Moses, shepherding in Midian, meets God in a bush that burns without being consumed. Asked for a name to give the Israelites, God answers "I AM WHO I AM," a name Israel later treated with great reverence.

quote.text: Now He is the first and supreme existence, who is altogether unchangeable, and who could say in the fullest sense of the words, “I AM That I AM,” and “Thou shalt say to them, I AM hath sent me unto you;”

steps.question: What does it mean to you that God's name speaks of being itself rather than of what God does?

steps.title: The Lord Is One
steps.intro: The Shema opens with a confession of the one Lord and a call to love him totally. Israel was to keep these words in heart, home and daily rhythm, as a way of living under the divine Name.

quote.text: Nor would the divine voice have said, Hear, O Israel, the Lord thy God is one God, unless Thou wert so a Trinity as to be one Lord God.

steps.question: Where could you place a daily reminder, like the Shema's, that God alone is the center of your life?

steps.title: How Wonderful Is Your Name
steps.intro: The psalm praises the divine Name as majestic across the whole earth, even as it marvels that God cares for humanity. Praise of the Name and wonder at human dignity are held together.

quote.text: I ask, how is His Name wonderful in all the earth? The answer is, “For Thy glory has been raised above the heavens.” So that the meaning is this, O Lord, who art our Lord, how do all that inhabit the earth admire Thee!

steps.question: What in creation most makes you want to praise God's name, and why?

steps.title: Hallowed Be Your Name
steps.intro: In the Lord's Prayer the first petition concerns the Name. Jesus teaches his disciples to begin prayer by asking that God's name be treated as holy, before turning to their own needs.

quote.text: After this we say, “Hallowed be Thy name;” not that we wish for God that He may be hallowed by our prayers, but that we beseech of Him that His name may be hallowed in us.

steps.question: How might your own conduct this week make God's name more honored among those who know you?

steps.title: The Light of the World
steps.intro: In the Temple, Jesus speaks in the first person with a series of "I am" sayings. Here he claims to be the light of the world, offering those who follow him the light of life.

quote.text: Therefore, my brethren, let us follow Christ, the light of the world, that we may not be walking in darkness.

steps.question: Where in your life do you most need light to walk by, and what would following look like?

steps.title: Before Abraham Was, I Am
steps.intro: Challenged about his relation to Abraham, Jesus answers with a present-tense claim: "before Abraham was, I am." Those listening take up stones, and Jesus leaves the Temple. The wording recalls the divine Name given to Moses.

quote.text: But wherefore said He not, “Before Abraham was, I was,” instead of “I Am”? As the Father useth this expression, “I Am,” so also doth Christ; for it signifieth continuous Being, irrespective of all time.

steps.question: Why might the plain words "I am" have sounded so startling to those hearing them?

steps.title: "I Am He"
steps.intro: In the garden, soldiers seek Jesus of Nazareth. He answers "I am he," and they draw back and fall to the ground. John presents Jesus handing himself over freely, not simply being seized.

quote.text: And Jesus did this to show, that not only they could not seize Him, but could not even see Him when in the midst, unless He gave permission.

steps.question: What does it change for you that Jesus walks into the Passion freely, with the Name on his lips?
